Hag.Description: The dress has seen better days, but still retains a semblance of the beauty that it once possessed, much like its wearer.
Wrapped in the remains of a boa constrictor, teeming with filth and moss—that which the swamp provides shall never be returned.
Her organs melted and fused into a burning mass.
Something, or someone, grew within her, its bones protruding, limbs reaching for freedom from the prison of flesh.
A deep outrage surged and stiffened her body, transforming her limbs into a hard, crust.
The smell alone was nearly enough to kill.
Insects had burrowed their way through her emaciated body.
Her grandmother told her a story of a moss-covered woman with a glowing heart.
Vegetation grew deep within her husk, tearing her apart in a beautiful red and green glow.
Exterior veins have developed across the surface of the skin, most likely supporting the twisted, snake-like protrusions from the side of the skull.
This hybrid reaction is also the start of the reproductive process, causing new, unexpected plant life to form.
The seed core is the central component in converting light into the chemical energy required to perform the key functions of a plant creature.
The mud has been wiped away and the Hag's hair is held off her face with rings and clips.
Ornamented of bone and blood, with teeth formed of the serpent. The result of one whose humanity has long been lost to rage and revenge.
Her charred dreads could not cover the painful, serum-filled blisters on her head.
The mark of power carved into her forehead allowed her to access unnatural abilities, but with it came a repulsive transformation.
Damp soil grumbled, and roots sprung from the ground.
Her face resembled a fish, her body almost human… a true horror from the depths.

Wraith.Description: A dark cape covering a dress suit, fastened with a mutilated angel that inspires both fear and respectability.
Did the roots grow out of him, or up from the earth?
Garbs taken from those who ventured too far from their home.
He has been wearing this old and tattered clothing for a while.
Rusted steel weaves and slices along his body, sharp edges scraping with each movement. It was the same fate as the victims he fed into the crusher, though they had been granted the mercy of death.
Rusted steel from an old vehicle abandoned in the swamp covered his flesh.
What was once good and pure now burned as an inferno within him. So hot, it would someday leave nothing but cold, dry ash.
What good is gold when your spirit is dead?
Extremely easy to see, except for when it isn’t.
Extremely easy to see, except for when it’s foggy.
He was amazed by the noble fabric.
One day, the strays clawed and meowed near a pile of metal scraps.
He ignored the flies buzzing around him as he removed the antlers from the deer and closed the trunk.
Wart-covered vest and waist wraps that move nimbly through pools of water and blood.
A once fine cloak now caked in the offal of his prey.
Embrace the cold, dark caress of the shadows for they are your only refuge.
A regal cloak that speaks to the wealth of its wearer.
A pale, crusted mask that conceals a dead, yellowed-fleshed face that no one dared to love. Until, perhaps…
A half-mask that fails to conceal the evil within.
A burlap sack with short sticks where the brain should be.
A sturdy mask made of bark that allowed him to venture in the woods undetected.
He blended in with the fog, with his pale and rough skin.
He returned from the spirit world, changed. The metal chains and plates fused into him, as if memories of his former life as a wrecker fused with his physical form.
He sought vengeance for his unjust fate as he waded through dirty water. Leathery fabric scraped the scales of his withered leather cloak.
Somewhere beneath the hood is conflict, uncertainty, and—most of all—rage.
The twin growths that burst from his skull caused a pain he could never forget.
While he should probably have had his helmet on, the sweltering heat made it worth taking a risk from time to time.
While he should probably have had his helmet on, the unending trials made it worth taking a risk from time to time.
A delicate piece of wool decorated with silver embroidery
The strays were always nearby, watching him, waiting.
He cringed at the putrid stench but was amazed by the impressive size of the perfectly symmetrical antlers.
A tattered, handmade cloak that removed a considerable amount of amphibians from the wetlands.

His chest heaved frantically. He struggled to catch his breath between choking peals of unbearable laughter.
The violence played out once again before his eyes. The laughter died a sudden death.
The nightmare faded from memory as he got out of bed. But one image remained clear in his mind: a gnarled bony tree.
Was it something he saw in his youth? The site of a profound pyre? He couldn't remember.
He didn't have time to think on it further. He had another long day at the scrapyard ahead of him.
A dancer was shoved to the ground by an unseen force. He returned to his feet and continued dancing as if nothing happened.
Another dancer fell, his head hitting the floor with a crack. Dancers swept back and forth, stepping in and out of the growing pool of blood.

Everything would be all right from now on, and his grandmother would always be with him.
